newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo Q1 above consensus, share climbs.
newsitem.headline: MoDo Q1 above consensus, share climbs.

text.p: Swedish forestry company Mo och Domsjo AB (MoDo) on Tuesday posted a slump in first quarter profits, saying lower market prices and unfavourable currency exchange hurt the result.
MoDo posted a profit of 391 million crowns after financial items compared to 858 in the same 1996 period. Sales edged down two percent to 5.46 billion crowns.
Currency hedging reduced the profit by 193 million crowns.
However, the company said higher delivery volumes also affected the result.
A Reuters survey showed analysts expected a pre-tax profit of 332 million crowns for the period. The share closed 10 crowns, or 4.5 percent, higher at 230 crowns.
MoDo said deliveries of pulp continued at a high level throughout the winter.

MoDo's pulp price increases, which are in line with recently announced rises by several producers, were likely to be carried out successfully, company chairman Bengt Pettersson told a news conference in connection with the results statement.
MoDo said earlier it planned to raise pulp to $580 per tonne from $520 from May 1.
"I believe this will go through even if there may be a little delay," Pettersson said.
The company described demand for fine paper as heavy in the first two months of the year but said market conditions slackened in March.
Higher newsprint capacity partly fuelled increased delivery volumes, although lower newsprint prices at the turn of the year had an impact, the company said.
